note: Frozen before A2/A3 results. S0 reproduces the original Deployment FAIL and is never rewritten; S1/S2 are conditional deployment scenarios.
lambda_policy: lambda is mapped to interpretable budgets, not an arbitrary weight: e.g. acceptable success loss per 100ms extra latency, or fallback quota. Raw success x latency Pareto frontier is reported alongside.

S0_current_cheap_fallback.definition: Current protocol cost weights (query 0.02, fallback 0.1, latency 0.01); fallback is cheap and always available.

S1_latency_budgeted.definition: Fallback available but subject to a hard latency/deadline budget: total decision+execution wall time must stay within T_budget; beyond budget the request is either aborted or downgraded to continue.
S1_latency_budgeted.constraint: T_budget scanning over {10s, 30s, 60s, 120s} decision-point incremental wall time (per 100ms acceptable success loss mapping)

S2_fallback_constrained.definition: Fallback unavailable, rate-limited, or callable for only a fraction of requests (quota q); counterfactual/resource-constraint scenario.
S2_fallback_constrained.baseline: quota-aware fallback (q fraction of units get fallback, rest continue)
S2_fallback_constrained.constraint: quota q scanning over {0.3, 0.5, 0.7}; never used to overturn S0 FAIL
S2_fallback_constrained.note: Only an anti-factual / resource-constraint scenario; cannot overturn S0 cheap-fallback FAIL.

deployment_pass_condition: In at least one preregistered scenario/budget interval, selector's CI lower bound is non-inferior to the target baseline AND it significantly reduces the constrained resource (latency or fallback calls); otherwise FAIL.
oracle_stop_rule: If the oracle upper bound cannot beat always-fallback under the preregistered budgets, close that scenario without tuning margin/model.
